turns.prompt_text: On terminal, how can I make the background translucent?
turns.response_html:
Adjusting terminal transparency (or translucency) depends entirely on which terminal emulator you are using, as the terminal is just an application running on your operating system.

Here is how to achieve this across the most common environments.

1. macOS (Native Terminal)

The default terminal on macOS has built-in support for Gaussian blur and transparency.

  1. Open Terminal.
  2. In the menu bar, go to Settings (or Cmd + ,).
  3. Select the Profiles tab.
  4. Click on the Text or Window sub-tab (depending on your macOS version).
  5. Click on Color & Effects.
  6. Adjust the Opacity slider to make it translucent and the Blur slider to keep the text readable against your wallpaper.

2. Windows (Windows Terminal)

If you are using the modern Windows Terminal (standard on Windows 11, downloadable on Windows 10), you can use "Acrylic" effects.

  1. Open Windows Terminal.
  2. Press Ctrl + Shift + , to open the Settings UI.
  3. Select your profile (e.g., PowerShell or Command Prompt) on the left sidebar.
  4. Go to Appearance.
  5. Scroll down to Transparency.
  6. Toggle Enable acrylic material and move the Background opacity slider to your preferred percentage.
  7. Click Save.

3. Linux (GNOME Terminal / Tilix / Alacritty)

On Linux, the method varies by desktop environment or specific app.

  • GNOME Terminal: Most modern versions have removed the transparency slider from the GUI. You may need to install a patched version or use a different terminal like Tilix or Guake, which still have the slider in Preferences > Profiles > Appearance.
  • Alacritty: This is a popular cross-platform terminal configured via a YAML or TOML file. You would edit your alacritty.toml file: 
    [window]
opacity = 0.8
  • i3 / Sway / KDE: If you use a tiling window manager or KDE Plasma, you can often force transparency on any window using the compositor settings (like Picom or the KWin blur effect).

4. Third-Party Power User Options (Cross-Platform)

If you want a highly customizable experience with easy transparency toggles, many developers prefer:

  • iTerm2 (macOS): Go to Profiles > Window > Transparency. It offers much better rendering than the default Mac terminal.
  • Warp: A modern, AI-integrated terminal that allows background images and transparency through its "Themes" settings.
  • Hyper: A terminal built on web technologies (Electron). You can add transparency by installing the hyper-opacity plugin or editing the .hyper.js CSS.
